title: PRINCE2 Foundation
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the PRINCE2 Foundation syllabus (principles, themes, processes, tailoring). Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: A project's business case shows that the expected benefits no longer justify the cost, but the project board has already authorised the next stage. According to the continued business justification principle, what should happen?
options: The project should be stopped or its scope changed because it no longer has a valid justification
The project should continue because the next stage was already authorised
The business case should be reviewed only once, at the end of the project
The business case should be dropped from the project board's regular agenda
items.explanation: Continued business justification means a PRINCE2 project must remain justifiable throughout, so if the benefits no longer justify the cost it should be re-scoped or stopped. An earlier authorisation does not override this, reviewing only at the end is too late, and removing the business case from governance removes the control.

items.stem: A project manager is about to start a project very similar to one completed last year by a different team. Which action best applies the learn from experience principle?
options: Begin planning from scratch so the new team is not influenced by old assumptions
Review lessons from the previous project and from the wider organization before planning
Wait until the first stage boundary before collecting any lessons
Ask the previous project board to run the new project instead
items.explanation: Learning from experience requires seeking relevant lessons at the start and throughout the project, so reviewing past projects before planning is correct. Starting from scratch discards useful knowledge, waiting until a stage boundary delays the benefit, and handing the project to the previous board does not capture lessons.

items.stem: A PRINCE2 project board has no one representing the interests of the people who will use and benefit from the final products. Which project board role is missing?
items.explanation: The senior user role represents those who will use the products and realise the benefits, so its absence leaves user interests unrepresented. The project manager and team manager are management roles, and project assurance monitors the project on the board's behalf rather than representing users.

items.stem: A long project is divided into management stages so the project board can review progress at fixed decision points and authorise work in chunks. Which PRINCE2 principle does this describe?
options: Tailor to suit the project environment
items.explanation: Manage by stages requires dividing the project into management stages with decision points where the board reviews and authorises the next stage. Manage by exception concerns tolerances, focus on products concerns product definitions, and tailoring concerns adapting the method to the environment.

items.stem: A project board delegates authority to a project manager but wants to be informed only when the project goes beyond agreed limits. Which principle does this illustrate?
items.explanation: Manage by exception means authority is delegated with tolerances and the next level of management is involved only if those tolerances are forecast to be exceeded. Manage by stages concerns decision points, and the other two principles concern justification and role clarity rather than escalation thresholds.

items.stem: A project team is spending a great deal of time listing activities but has never agreed what the final deliverable must contain or how it will be judged. Which PRINCE2 principle is being ignored?
items.explanation: Focus on products requires defining and agreeing the products, their quality criteria and their purpose before planning the work, so failing to define the deliverable ignores it. The other principles concern justification, learning and tolerances, none of which address the missing product definition.

items.stem: A small, low-risk project is being run with exactly the same heavyweight documentation and controls as a large compliance programme. Which PRINCE2 principle is not being applied?
options: Tailor to suit the project environment
items.explanation: Tailor to suit the project environment means the method's processes, products and controls are scaled to the project's size, complexity and risk. Applying heavy controls to a small project shows no tailoring, and the other principles concern stages, roles and products rather than proportionality.

items.stem: Which statement best describes how the seven PRINCE2 principles should be applied to a project?
options: They are optional recommendations that a project manager may ignore
They apply only to large projects run in a formal environment
They should be applied unless the project board votes to suspend one
They must all be applied for the project to be PRINCE2, although how they are applied can be tailored
items.explanation: The principles are mandatory and must all be applied to qualify as a PRINCE2 project, but the method used to apply them can be tailored. They cannot be voted away or ignored, and they apply to projects of every size and environment.

items.stem: Which PRINCE2 theme provides the mechanism to judge whether the project is desirable, viable and achievable at each stage?
items.explanation: The business case theme establishes the business justification and is reviewed at each stage to confirm the project remains desirable, viable and achievable. Organization covers roles, plans covers how work is scheduled, and progress covers monitoring and control.

items.stem: In PRINCE2, which project board role is ultimately accountable for the business case throughout the project?
items.explanation: The executive is accountable for the business case and owns it on behalf of the project board. The senior user represents user interests and benefits, the senior supplier represents those creating the products, and the project manager prepares and maintains the business case but is not ultimately accountable for it.

items.stem: A project has delivered all of its products, but the expected benefits will only become measurable after the project has closed. What should be recorded to support this?
options: An exception report to the project board
A post-project benefits review in the benefits management approach
A fresh project mandate for a follow-on project
items.explanation: The benefits management approach states how and when benefits will be measured and reviewed, including post-project reviews. A project mandate starts a new project, an exception report addresses tolerance breaches, and a product breakdown structure describes products rather than benefits.

items.stem: Which PRINCE2 project board role represents the suppliers who will create the project's specialist products?
items.explanation: The senior supplier role represents the interests of those designing and creating the products, including their capability and resources. The senior user represents users, the executive owns the business case, and the project manager manages delivery on the board's behalf.

items.stem: The project board wants independent monitoring of the project's quality, progress and risks on its behalf. Which role provides this?
items.explanation: Project assurance monitors the project independently on behalf of the project board and reports any concerns. The team manager runs a team, project support provides administrative services, and the senior supplier is a board member representing supplier interests.

items.stem: Who is responsible for the day-to-day management of a PRINCE2 project and for delivering its products within the agreed constraints?
items.explanation: The project manager runs the project day to day and is responsible for delivering the products within the tolerances agreed with the project board. The executive and senior user are board roles, and project assurance monitors rather than manages delivery.

items.stem: Which PRINCE2 theme defines the customer's quality expectations and the standards that the project's products must meet?
items.explanation: The quality theme captures the customer's quality expectations and defines the quality criteria, quality methods and acceptance criteria for products. Plans, change and progress address scheduling, issue control and monitoring respectively.

items.stem: Where are a product's quality criteria, quality tolerance and quality method documented in PRINCE2?
items.explanation: A product description records the product's purpose, composition, quality criteria, quality method and quality tolerance. The project brief and business case summarise the project, and an exception report escalates a tolerance breach.

items.stem: A quality review is planned to check whether a product conforms to its quality criteria. Which set of roles should be arranged for the review?
options: Roles such as chair, presenter, reviewer and approver as appropriate
Any available member of the project board
Only the person who produced the product
items.explanation: A PRINCE2 quality review uses defined roles such as chair, presenter, reviewers and approver to give a structured, independent assessment. A single person, the producer alone, or arbitrary board members would not provide the required balance and independence.

items.stem: Which PRINCE2 plan covers the entire project and gives the project board an overall view of scope, cost and timescales?
items.explanation: The project plan is the high-level plan for the whole project and is used by the project board to understand overall scope, cost and timescales. Team plans and stage plans cover narrower slices of work, and the benefits management approach describes benefits realisation.

items.stem: When does a PRINCE2 project manager normally create the next stage plan?
options: During initiating a project, for every stage at once
During managing a stage boundary, before that stage starts
At the very end of the project during closing a project
items.explanation: The next stage plan is prepared during the managing a stage boundary process so the project board can authorise the stage before it begins. Planning every stage up front defeats manage by stages, and preparing it during closure or while controlling the current stage is too early or too late.

items.stem: Which planning technique is central to PRINCE2 and begins by identifying the products that the project must deliver?
items.explanation: Product-based planning is the PRINCE2 technique that defines the products first, using a product breakdown structure and product descriptions, before deriving activities. Critical path analysis, earned value and rolling wave planning are scheduling or control techniques, not PRINCE2's product-first planning technique.

items.stem: Which PRINCE2 theme addresses the uncertainty that could affect the project's objectives, whether it is a threat or an opportunity?
items.explanation: The risk theme covers uncertainty that could affect objectives and explicitly includes both threats and opportunities. Change covers issues and modifications, progress covers monitoring, and quality covers product conformance.

items.stem: Where are a project's risk procedures, such as the risk categories and the risk tolerance, documented in PRINCE2?
items.explanation: The risk management approach records how risk will be managed, including procedures, risk categories, scales and tolerance. The risk register holds individual risks, the issue register holds issues, and the project brief is a pre-project summary.

items.stem: In PRINCE2, what is the term for the person responsible for the management, monitoring and control of a particular risk?
items.explanation: The risk owner is responsible for managing, monitoring and controlling a specific risk. The risk actionee carries out the agreed response but does not own the risk, while project assurance and the senior supplier are unrelated roles.

items.stem: In PRINCE2, a request for change, an off-specification and a problem or concern are all types of what?
items.explanation: PRINCE2 groups requests for change, off-specifications and problems or concerns under the single heading of issues. Risks are uncertain future events, an exception is a tolerance breach, and a change proposal is not the generic PRINCE2 term used in the change theme.

items.stem: Where does PRINCE2 record how issues and changes will be identified, assessed and controlled on the project?
items.explanation: The change control approach defines how issues and changes are identified, assessed, prioritised and controlled. The issue register records the individual issues, configuration item records track products, and the daily log is the project manager's personal log.

items.stem: Which PRINCE2 activity tracks the versions and status of the project's products and controls changes to them?
items.explanation: Configuration management identifies products, controls changes to them, records their status and verifies their completeness. Risk management handles uncertainty, progress control monitors performance, and quality control checks conformance rather than product versions and status.

items.stem: A project board sets tolerances for time, cost, scope, risk, quality and benefit. What is the main purpose of these tolerances?
options: To remove the need for any progress reporting to the board
To set the personal performance objectives of the project manager
To define the limits of delegated authority within which the project manager can manage
To guarantee that the project will finish on time and within budget
items.explanation: Tolerances define the permissible deviation from plan within which a level of management may act before escalating, enabling manage by exception. They do not guarantee outcomes, they require reporting rather than remove it, and they are not personal performance objectives.

items.stem: A project manager forecasts that the current stage will exceed the agreed stage time tolerance. What should the project manager do?
options: Quietly adjust the stage plan to hide the deviation
Ask the team to work unpaid overtime to recover the schedule
Take no action and continue until the stage ends
Produce an exception report and escalate to the project board
items.explanation: Under manage by exception, a forecast breach of stage tolerance must be escalated to the project board with an exception report so it can decide how to proceed. Ignoring or hiding the deviation breaches governance, and unpaid overtime is not an acceptable control response.

items.stem: Which PRINCE2 product gives the project manager a regular summary of the progress of work being carried out by a team manager?
items.explanation: The team manager sends checkpoint reports to the project manager at agreed intervals to summarise the progress of a work package. Highlight reports go from the project manager to the board, end stage reports close a stage, and exception reports cover tolerance breaches.

items.stem: Which PRINCE2 report does the project manager send to the project board at agreed intervals to summarise the progress of a stage?
items.explanation: The highlight report is the project manager's periodic summary to the project board on stage progress. Checkpoint reports flow upward from team managers, the end project report closes the project, and exception reports are produced only when tolerances are threatened.

items.stem: Which PRINCE2 process is triggered by a project mandate and produces the project brief?
items.explanation: Starting up a project is the pre-project process triggered by a mandate that produces the project brief and the plan for the initiation stage. Initiating a project builds the PID, directing a project is the board's process, and controlling a stage manages a live stage.

items.stem: Which document is created during starting up a project to give the project board enough information to decide whether to initiate the project?
items.explanation: The project brief provides the pre-project information on which the board bases its authorise-initiation decision. The full project plan and business case are developed during initiating a project, and an end stage report is produced at the end of a stage.

items.stem: In the starting up a project process, which role is responsible for appointing the project manager?
items.explanation: During starting up a project the executive and project board are appointed, and the board appoints the project manager. Team managers are appointed later, project assurance is a board responsibility, and the senior supplier is a board member rather than the appointing authority for the project manager.

items.stem: Which PRINCE2 process is performed by the project board and includes authorising the project and the start of each stage?
items.explanation: Directing a project is the project board's process and includes authorising initiation, authorising the project, authorising stages or exception plans, giving ad hoc direction and confirming closure. The other processes are performed by the project manager, team manager or those supporting them.

items.stem: After the project manager has prepared the project initiation documentation, what does the project board do within the directing a project process?
items.explanation: Once the PID is ready the board's authorise-the-project activity approves the project and commits resources. The mandate predates the project, product descriptions are prepared by the project manager, and team managers are appointed by the project manager, not the board.

items.stem: A significant external event affects the project midway through a stage. Which directing a project activity lets the project board respond and give direction at any time?
options: Authorise a stage or exception plan
items.explanation: Give ad hoc direction allows the board to respond to information such as highlight or exception reports and provide guidance at any time. Authorising plans and the project and confirming closure are discrete decisions rather than an ongoing channel for direction.

items.stem: Which activity in the directing a project process is performed by the project board at the very end of the project?
items.explanation: Confirm project closure is the board's final directing a project decision, taken after the project manager recommends closure. Authorising the project happens near the start, and authorising work packages is a project manager activity in controlling a stage.

items.stem: Which PRINCE2 process develops the project brief into the project plan and full business case before the project is authorised?
items.explanation: Initiating a project turns the project brief into the project initiation documentation, including the project plan, business case and approaches. Starting up produces the brief, managing a stage boundary plans the next stage, and closing a project ends the project.

items.stem: Which PRINCE2 product is the consolidated set of information that describes the project and forms the baseline for its management?
items.explanation: The project initiation documentation is the consolidated baseline of the project, covering the business case, plans, approaches and controls. The mandate is the pre-project trigger, a work package assigns work, and a product description defines a single product.

items.stem: During initiating a project, which product describes how and when the project's benefits will be measured and reviewed?
items.explanation: The benefits management approach defines the benefit measurements, reviews and responsibilities. The business case justifies the project, the end project report summarises performance at closure, and the quality management approach covers quality controls rather than benefit realisation.

items.stem: Which process does the project manager carry out day to day to assign work packages and monitor their progress?
items.explanation: Controlling a stage is the project manager's day-to-day process for authorising work packages, monitoring progress and handling issues and risks. Managing product delivery is the team manager's process, managing a stage boundary ends a stage, and initiating a project sets the project up.

items.stem: In controlling a stage, what is the agreement called by which the project manager assigns work to a team manager?
items.explanation: A work package is the agreement between the project manager and team manager for the delivery of one or more products. A product description defines a product, the stage plan covers the whole stage, and the quality register tracks quality activities.

items.stem: While controlling a stage, how does the project manager decide whether corrective action is needed?
options: By asking the project board to check progress every day
By relying only on the team manager's verbal updates
By reviewing progress against the stage plan and taking action as required
By waiting until the stage boundary to compare results
items.explanation: Controlling a stage requires regularly reviewing actual progress against the stage plan so deviation is detected and corrected early. Waiting until the stage boundary is too late, daily board checks are unworkable, and unverified verbal updates are not adequate control.

items.stem: While controlling a stage, a team manager raises an issue that affects the stage plan but remains within stage tolerance. What should the project manager do?
options: Immediately escalate it to the project board as an exception
Ignore it until the stage boundary
Ask the project board to replan the whole project
Manage the issue within the stage and update the relevant registers
items.explanation: An issue within stage tolerance is handled by the project manager, who takes corrective action and updates the issue and risk registers. Escalating within tolerance undermines manage by exception, ignoring the issue is negligent, and replanning the project is disproportionate.

items.stem: Which process is performed by the team manager to accept, execute and deliver a work package?
items.explanation: Managing product delivery is the team manager's process, with the activities accept a work package, execute a work package and deliver a work package. Controlling a stage and directing a project are project manager and board processes, and managing a stage boundary closes a stage.

items.stem: In managing product delivery, which activity involves the team manager and project manager agreeing the work and its requirements before work starts?
items.explanation: Accept a work package is the managing product delivery activity in which the team manager agrees the work package and its requirements with the project manager. Authorising a work package belongs to controlling a stage, and execute and deliver follow once the work is accepted.

items.stem: In managing product delivery, when does the team manager seek approval that the completed work package conforms to its requirements?
options: Never, because the team approves its own work
Before any work on the package begins
At the point of delivering the completed work package
Only at the end of the whole project
items.explanation: Deliver a work package is the activity in which the team manager confirms the work is complete and seeks the project manager's approval. Approval before work is done is premature, project-end approval is too late, and teams cannot self-approve their delivery.

items.stem: Which PRINCE2 process provides the project board with the information it needs to assess whether the project remains viable and to authorise the next stage?
items.explanation: Managing a stage boundary produces the end stage report, next stage plan and updated business case and project plan so the board can decide whether to continue. Controlling a stage runs the current stage, directing a project makes board decisions, and initiating a project sets the project up.

items.stem: At the end of a stage, which product does the project manager produce to summarise the stage's performance and inform the next stage plan?
items.explanation: The end stage report summarises performance against the stage plan and supports the board's decision on the next stage. The end project report closes the project, checkpoint reports cover work package progress, and exception reports cover tolerance breaches.

items.stem: A project is forecast to exceed its project tolerances. What does the project manager produce during managing a stage boundary, at the project board's request?
items.explanation: When project tolerances are threatened and the board requests it, the project manager produces an exception plan showing how the project will recover, for the board's approval. An exception report raises the deviation, an end stage report covers normal stage closure, and a team plan is a lower-level schedule.

items.stem: Which product is prepared during managing a stage boundary so that the project board can authorise the start of the next stage?
items.explanation: The next stage plan sets out the work, products and resources for the next stage so the board can authorise it. The mandate is a pre-project input, the daily log is the project manager's personal record, and a product status account reports configuration status.

items.stem: Which process is used to confirm that the project's products have been accepted and that there is nothing left to deliver?
items.explanation: Closing a project confirms that products have been accepted, evaluates the project and recommends closure. Managing a stage boundary is for intermediate stages, managing product delivery delivers work packages, and controlling a stage manages an active stage.

items.stem: Which product, produced during closing a project, evaluates how the project performed against its baselines and records lessons for the organization?
items.explanation: The end project report reviews performance against the project's baselines, confirms acceptance and captures lessons. The end stage report covers a single stage, while highlight and checkpoint reports are periodic progress reports produced earlier in the project.

items.stem: During closing a project, which activity ensures that the project's products have been handed over and accepted by the customer?
options: Hand over products and obtain acceptance
items.explanation: Closing a project includes handing over the products and confirming customer acceptance before closure is recommended. Authorising the project and creating a brief happen at the start, and appointing the project manager is a starting up a project activity.

items.stem: An organization wants PRINCE2 to become its normal way of running projects rather than a method used for just one project. What is this called?
items.explanation: Embedding PRINCE2 means adopting it into the organization's standard ways of working so it becomes routine, not a one-off. A mandate starts a project, an exception plan addresses a tolerance breach, and a quality review assesses a product.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Foundation syllabus - Tailoring and the PRINCE2 Environment

items.stem: A PRINCE2 project is small and low risk. How should the project manager apply the method?
options: Ignore PRINCE2 because it only fits large projects
Add extra management products to be safe
Apply the full PRINCE2 method without any change
Tailor the method so the processes and products are proportionate to the project
items.explanation: PRINCE2 should be tailored to the project's scale and risk so that controls and products are proportionate. Applying the full method unchanged ignores tailoring, abandoning PRINCE2 is unnecessary since it suits all sizes, and adding unneeded products wastes effort.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Foundation syllabus - Tailoring and the PRINCE2 Environment

items.stem: Which statement best describes how PRINCE2 should be tailored to suit a project's environment?
options: The method is adapted while keeping all seven principles intact
The principles can be dropped when the schedule is tight
Tailoring means removing every management product
Only the project board may tailor the method
items.explanation: Tailoring adapts the processes, themes and products to the environment, but the seven principles are mandatory and cannot be removed. Dropping principles means the work is no longer PRINCE2, removing all products removes governance, and tailoring is not reserved to the board.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Foundation syllabus - Tailoring and the PRINCE2 Environment

items.stem: An organization adopts PRINCE2 but does not change its existing reporting and governance, and staff rarely use the method. What is the most likely reason?
options: PRINCE2 is inherently unusable in practice
PRINCE2 was not properly embedded in the organization's ways of working
The project managers did not work enough overtime
All the projects were too small for any method
items.explanation: Embedding requires aligning PRINCE2 with existing governance, reporting and culture so it becomes how work is done. Overtime and project size are irrelevant to adoption, and PRINCE2 is widely used, so the likely cause is poor embedding.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Foundation syllabus - Tailoring and the PRINCE2 Environment

items.stem: A very short, two-week project is being planned. What is the most appropriate way to apply PRINCE2's management stages?
options: Ask the project board to define a new stage every week
Use no stages at all because the project is short
Use a single or minimal number of stages proportionate to the project
Always create at least six management stages
items.explanation: The number of management stages is tailored to the project, so a short project may sensibly have one or very few. Using no stages removes the control points, imposing six stages is disproportionate, and weekly stages would create overhead without benefit.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Foundation syllabus - Tailoring and the PRINCE2 Environment

items.stem: Which part of the project documentation records how PRINCE2 has been tailored for the project, including adjustments to processes and products?
options: The tailoring section of the project initiation documentation
items.explanation: The project initiation documentation records the tailoring decisions, showing how the method has been adapted for the project. The mandate is the pre-project trigger, the daily log is a personal record, and the quality register tracks planned quality activities.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Foundation syllabus - Tailoring and the PRINCE2 Environment
